next_round_constraints: Prioritize observation_map='delayed_I' with delay_weeks constrained to {0,1} (keep 2+ weeks out unless exploring a specific hypothesis).
Focus search on SEIR and SEIRS families; avoid SEIHR variants for this series unless the observation is not H-based and parameter count is tightly controlled.
Keep model complexity minimal (no extra compartments beyond what is needed); prefer configurations that are stable across rolling splits over those that only improve a single validation window.
If exploring SEIRS, constrain waning/reinfection effects to be weak/slow (i.e., avoid aggressive cycling behavior) to prevent spurious oscillations on short training data.
observed_failure_modes: Hospitalization-rate target is best matched by infectious-incidence proxy with a short reporting/admission lag (delayed_I); explicit hospitalization compartment observation (H or I+H) underperforms and is less stable across rolling splits.

Peakiness is high; simpler SEIR/SEIRS with delayed observation captures peaks better than adding H dynamics, suggesting over-parameterization/identifiability issues for SEIHR on this series length (31 train weeks).
Delay sensitivity appears modest but favors ~1 week; extending to 2 weeks slightly degrades fit, indicating the effective lag is short and should not be pushed longer without strong justification.

SEIRS provides only marginal improvement over SEIR, implying reinfection/waning immunity may not be strongly identifiable in this short window; added complexity risks unnecessary penalty without consistent gain.
feedback.proposer_instruction: For the next round on 'Overall', propose a small set of low-complexity templates centered on SEIR/SEIRS with observation_map='delayed_I'. Treat delay as a tuning knob but keep it at 0–1 week (1 week as the default). Do not propose H-observed SEIHR or I+H observation variants. If you include SEIRS, constrain it to behave close to SEIR (slow waning) to avoid overfitting and instability on 31 training points.
